text:
Gabriel Vilardi lives in front of the net, and so far the net has not been kind. He has three goals on 8.53 expected, shooting 5.9%, when our range for his true rate runs 12.1% to 16.8%. That is the kind of gap that tends to close, because the chances keep coming.

Winnipeg has noticed. His ice time is up to 20:16 over his last ten games, and he has 10 points in that stretch, including the late equalizer in Chicago and two assists in the overtime win over the Islanders. Thirteen of his 16 points are assists, eight on the power play.

The style is the same as ever. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.4 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in 2025-26, 99th percentile among forwards, and Evolving-Hockey rated him 2.4 wins above replacement, 34th among forwards. NHL Edge puts his top speed in the 4th percentile, which says plenty about how he gets there: positioning, not pace. Our numbers project 66 points and 21 goals.
headline: Vilardi gets the looks; the goals are late
